title: Juicy Japanese Pork Gyoza
description: A traditional Japanese dish featuring pan-fried dumplings filled with pork and vegetables, served with a dipping sauce. This recipe uses 00-flour for a delicate crust and is FODMAP-friendly.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground pork, chopped cabbage, green onions, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, salt, and black pepper, and mix well with your hands until just combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the 00-flour and a pinch of salt.
Gradually add water to the flour mixture and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into small balls, about the size of a small egg.
Roll out each ball of dough into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of the pork filling in the center of each dough circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape and press the edges together to seal the gyoza.
Heat a large skillet with a small amount of oil over medium-high heat and pan-fry the gyoza until they are golden brown on the bottom.
Add a small amount of water to the skillet and cover with a lid to steam the gyoza until they are cooked through.
Serve the gyoza hot with a dipping sauce made from soy sauce and sesame oil.
